title: What Actually Happens When You Press Ctrl+Z?
sources: Mercury blog, 'The undo button and the history of modern computing' (2026): each subsequent Undo takes the user further back in the undo stack / command history; once you do something new you can't redo what was undone; Warren Teitelman discussed Undo in 1966, FRESS (1968) first implemented it; Ctrl-Z attributed to Larry Tesler and the Apple Lisa in 1983

Larry Tesler email quoted in 'The Origins of Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Ctrl+X, and Ctrl+Z Explained': 'The Lisa was the first system to assign XCVZ to cut, copy, paste and undo'; Z was chosen because it is next to X, C and V on the US QWERTY keyboard, in the lower-left corner near the modifier keys so one hand can press them
University of Washington CSE 340 undo lab: undo pops the last action off the undo stack and reverses it, undone actions go onto a redo stack, and taking a new action clears the redo stack
Apple Developer, Undo Manager (Cocoa Undo Architecture): apps record undo operations on an undo stack and undone operations on a redo stack

lines.text: What actually happens when you press Control Z?
Every time you type, delete or move something,
your app writes it down on a hidden list,
lines.caps: YOUR APP *WRITES | IT *DOWN | ON A *HIDDEN LIST

lines.text: stacked like plates, with the newest on top.
Undo just lifts the top plate off and reverses it,
lines.caps: *UNDO JUST | *LIFTS | THE *TOP PLATE | OFF AND *REVERSES IT

lines.text: and every extra press goes one more step back.
But those plates aren't thrown away.
They wait on a second pile,
and that's what redo puts back.
Do anything new, and that redo pile gets wiped.
lines.caps: DO ANYTHING *NEW | AND THAT *REDO | PILE GETS *WIPED

lines.text: In nineteen eighty-three, Apple's Lisa put it next to X, C and V,
lines.caps: IN *1983 | APPLE'S *LISA | PUT IT *NEXT TO | *X, C | AND *V

lines.text: so one hand reaches them all.
So Control Z isn't magic. It's just a stack of plates.
lines.caps: SO CONTROL *Z | ISN'T *MAGIC | IT'S JUST A *STACK | OF *PLATES
